conviction_note: Q3 revenue is already public and about 2% above the top of guide, so the room is in Q3 margin (probably at or above the top of 65-67%, with FX neutral at a Q3 average near 32.0) and in the Q4 guide. The sell-side bar has already moved up to Q3 GM 67.3-67.5% and Q4 GM 68.1% / revenue +12.5% q/q. This week the tape is selling good semiconductor prints: ASML raised its guide today and fell, and TSM's last print sold off 3.8% on a capex raise. The findings net to -0.4 and the scaled number is (2*0.48-1)*4.5 = -0.18: a near-coin-flip lean, because the fundamental read is mildly positive and the reaction function is mildly negative.
bar: Q3 net profit consensus NT$746.3bn (LSEG SmartEstimate, 16 analysts; https://www.tikr.com/blog/tsmcs-q3-earnings-preview-65-profit-growth-but-net-margin-seen-slipping-to-50, 2026-10-12), with the Q3 company guide GM 65-67% and OM 56-58% at NT$32/USD (https://investor.tsmc.com/quarterly-results). Q4 revenue bar is about US$52bn from two broadly agreeing sources: consensus +54% YoY on Q4'25 US$33.73bn (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/14/history-says-this-happens-to-taiwan-semiconductor/ plus https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000104617926000008/a4q25e_withguidancexfinal.htm) and Morgan Stanley +10-15% q/q (https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview). The Q4 GM bar of 68.1% has a single source (Yuanta, https://ec.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5602509), so the finding that depends on it is capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is my estimate of Q3 net profit against the LSEG figure.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 33.4m ADS, roughly 0.5% of float, with about 2.3 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 settlement, the latest I found (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/tsm/short-interest/). It is not crowded and no squeeze mechanism is visible. The baseline 25-delta skew is -1.82 vol points: calls are slightly bid and the market's lean is 'balanced'. The put/call OI ratio is 1.37. The ADR is -8.5% over 5 days and -11% from its 52-week high ($485.80 record close on 2026-10-05 per Admiral). Retail sentiment on Stocktwits moved from bullish to neutral (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/asml-tsmc-report-week-traders-033013514.html, 2026-10-13).

findings.finding: Q3 revenue from the monthly reports is NT$1,494.2bn, 1.95% above the top of guide at NT$32. The Q3 average USD/TWD was close to the 32.0 assumption (July ~32.0-32.45, August 32.3 falling to 31.6, September ~31.5-31.9), so there is no material FX hit to margin. On the Q2 precedent (revenue at the top of guide, GM 67.7% against a 65.5-67.5% guide), Q3 GM is likely 67-68% against the 65-67% guide, which puts net profit a few percent above the LSEG NT$746.3bn consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TSM has sold its beats: the Motley Fool (2026-10-14) says the stock declined or was weak after three of the last four reports despite EPS beats. The July 2026 print, with GM 67.7% above guide, moved -3.8% (Admiral Markets, 2026-10-12).
findings.why_not_priced: The LSEG net profit consensus (NT$746.3bn, about a 50% net margin) and the Hudson Labs GM consensus of 66.5% sit at or near the guide midpoint and look stale against the pre-released revenue. If this were fully priced, consensus would read 67.5%+ GM and about NT$770bn of net profit. It is partly priced: Yuanta already moved Q3 GM to 67.3% and Morgan Stanley is at 67.5%.
findings.independence: The Q2 actuals (US$40.20bn against a 39.0-40.2 guide, GM 67.7%) are at https://www.storagenewsletter.com/2026/07/22/tsmc-fiscal-2q26-financial-results/. The FX series is from Focus Taiwan daily closes (https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202607310016, https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202608280016, https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202609290010). Yuanta's 67.3% (https://ec.ltn.com.tw/article/breakingnews/5602509) points the same way. The revenue figure shares its document with the sweep row's TrendForce source.

findings.finding: ASML, TSMC's most direct supplier, reported on 2026-10-14, after TSMC last spoke in July. It said its planned supply for 2027 and 2028 'will not fully meet the demand of our customers', that customers are expressing interest in 2029-2030 orders, and that long-term advance customer payments rose €5.7bn in the quarter to €9.3bn. It raised FY26 sales to €44-45bn, with Taiwan, Korea and the US taking 76% of Q3 system sales. This corroborates a strong demand and 2027 capex message from TSMC.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July 2026 the 2026 capex raise to $60-64bn (about 14% above the prior range) coincided with a -3.8% reaction, and Insider Monkey attributes the selloff to spending. A large 2027 capex signal has therefore been read negatively by TSM holders.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since this morning, but TSM fell about 3% today (spot 431.985 at 17:07 UTC against a 445.12 close on 10-13) rather than rising on it. That means the market either reads it as capex-negative for TSM or is not transmitting it into TSM. If priced as demand-positive, TSM would have rallied with an ASML guide raise.
findings.independence: The CNBC headline (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/14/asml-3q-earnings-ai-demand-orders-capacity.html, 403 on fetch, title only) and the Yahoo/Stocktwits ASML piece say the same. Hock Tan (Broadcom, 2026-10-12) called compute demand 'insatiable' through 2030 (https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/10/12/broadcom-ceo-says-biggest-hurdle-in-ai-fuelled-tech-growth-is-capital-not-memory-chips). The positive sign is held small because finding 4 shows the market sold this same ASML document.

findings.finding: The 5-day -8.5% drawdown was driven by sector items TSMC is not exposed to: CXMT's DRAM claim knocked SK Hynix -9% (TSMC makes no DRAM), and Broadcom's Hock Tan said capital, not wafers or memory, is AI's constraint. That leaves the bar into the print lower without a TSMC-specific cause.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean precedent. The July print came after a run-up to the high and sold off.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly by definition: the drawdown is in the baseline. The only unpriced part is that the cause is not TSMC's. If the market had separated TSMC from the memory scare, TSM would not have fallen with SOXX for six sessions.
findings.independence: The Yahoo/Stocktwits sector piece (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/asml-tsmc-report-week-traders-033013514.html) lists the same causes. This is an inference about positioning, so it is sized small (lesson 5).

findings.finding: The tape is selling good semiconductor prints this week. ASML raised its FY26 guide and topped Q4 consensus at the high end, yet fell about 2-3% (US overnight -3%, Reuters-cited -1.86%), and the selloff spread to MU, SNDK and INTC. TSM sold its last print -3.8% and was weak after three of its last four beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 -3.8% after a beat with a capex raise (Admiral Markets). The Fool says three of the last four reactions were down or weak despite beats.
findings.why_not_priced: The option market prices it as balanced (skew -1.82, calls slightly bid), so it does not lean on this reaction pattern. If the market were pricing a sell-the-news reaction, puts would be bid.
findings.independence: Admiral Markets gives the -3.8% last-print move (https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview). The Fool's three-of-four pattern is at https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/14/history-says-this-happens-to-taiwan-semiconductor/. The ASML reaction sources disagree on size (CNBC said +2% early in Europe), which caps this finding at -1.0. Short interest is 0.5% of float, so no squeeze offsets it.

findings.finding: The Taiwanese sell-side has moved the Q4 bar above what management's dilution commentary implies. Yuanta has Q4 revenue at NT$1,662.5bn (+12.5% q/q) and Q4 GM at 68.1%, raised from 67.8%. The CFO guided 3-4 points of 2nm dilution in H2 plus overseas-fab dilution of 2-3 points that widens to 3-4 later, and the TWD in October (~31.78-31.90) is about 0.5% stronger than Q3's ~32.0 average, roughly a 0.2-point GM headwind. A Q4 GM guide centred near 67% would read as a miss against that bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July a Q3 GM guide of 65-67% (down from 67.7%) was called a 'modest disappointment' by Barclays, and the stock fell 3.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: US-wire consensus (Hudson 66.5% for Q3) has no Q4 GM number. If the market were alert to a high Q4 margin bar, the US previews would quote it. The bar has one source, so the finding is capped small (lesson 6).
findings.independence: The dilution comments are at https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/07/16/news-tsmc-lifts-2026-capex-15-to-60-64b-hikes-sales-outlook-to-over-40-despite-q3-margin-dip/ (2026-07-16). October FX is from Focus Taiwan (https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202610120015). The Q4 revenue bar of about $52bn is consistent between the Fool (+54% YoY) and Morgan Stanley (+10-15% q/q), so only the GM part is single-sourced.

findings.finding: Nikkei reported in July, unconfirmed by TSMC, that 2027 wafer prices rise 5-10% on advanced nodes, with a 10-15% premium on HPC orders above forecast. A confirmation on the call would support the 2027 GM path (Yuanta 69%) that the market is debating.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The report itself was July news, with no clean stock reaction attributable to it.
findings.source_date: 2026-07 (per CRN Asia and Malaysian Wireless URL paths /2026/07/)
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, being three months old and widely reported. The unpriced part is company confirmation. If it were fully priced, 2027 GM estimates would already sit at 69-70% across the street rather than in one broker.
findings.independence: https://www.malaysianwireless.com/2026/07/tsmc-chip-price-increase-2027/ and https://www.crnasia.com/news/2026/components-and-peripherals/tsmc-s-2027-price-rise-could-drive-up-costs-for-everything both rest on the same Nikkei report, so they count once.

outside_window.finding: The full 2027 capex and revenue outlook is normally given in January, not at the October call. Sell-side 2027 capex estimates range $75-90bn (MS 75-80, Citi 81, GS 85, UBS 90), so the October call should give direction only.

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced (-1.82, calls slightly bid) and the run-up is -8.5% over 5 days. My slight negative lean comes from the reaction function, not the fundamentals, so it cuts mildly against the call-bid skew and the oversold run-up. That is why p_up sits at 48, not lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; TSM sells its beats): finding 1 (Q3 GM/EPS above consensus) cut from +0.6 to +0.3.
Lesson 5 (the absence of a company cause is not evidence of overreaction): finding 3 (drawdown from a memory scare TSMC does not face) cut from +0.5 to +0.2.
Lesson 6 (a single-source bar caps the finding): finding 5 (Q4 GM bar 68.1%, Yuanta only) cut from -0.6 to -0.4.
Lesson 3 (a caveat must reach the number): finding 2 (ASML corroboration) cut from +0.4 to +0.3, because the market sold the same ASML document today.
Core step 2 / lesson 5 (file sourced proxies rather than leaving them out): added finding 6, the 2027 wafer price increase report, at +0.2. It was not in the draft.

Lesson 'asking what the market missed generates pessimism': p_up held at 48, not lowered further. abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5 because the hunters' moves have run too small and a Q4 guide plus 2027 capex direction is new information.
The sweep's untrustworthy-history flag: the base rate was rebuilt from the July print (-3.8%) and the Fool's three-of-four statement; the 6-K monthly history was not used.
